prompt:
Create one abstract magical ORB representing a Level 1 Dungeons & Dragons spell slot.

This image belongs to an experimental coherent series of nine spell-slot images. All nine must unmistakably belong to the same family: one centered orb suspended in a cloudy, painterly nebular field. The orb must always be clearly visible and substantial; Level 1 is NOT a tiny seed.

## Full series progression — use this to create contrast
1 — Awakening: increasing complexity.
2 — Coalescence: increasing complexity.
3 — Ignition: increasing complexity.
4 — Convergence: increasing complexity.
5 — Ascendance: increasing complexity.
6 — Apotheosis: maximum visible complexity, electric-blue apex.
7 — Transcendence: greater power through decreasing complexity and darker atmosphere.
8 — Event Horizon: greater power through decreasing complexity and darker atmosphere.
9 — Totality: absolute simplicity, pure-black totality.

Complexity rises deliberately from Levels 1 through 6. Level 6 is the visual-complexity apex. Levels 7, 8 and 9 represent MORE POWER with progressively LESS visual complexity. Level 9 is the final revelation: cosmic simplicity comparable to the majesty of total solar eclipse totality.

## Full color progression
1 #DED7C5 — dirty eggshell / warm ivory; 2 #E8C66A — pale golden yellow; 3 #E85A2A — saturated orange-red; 4 #F29C24 — intense amber-gold; 5 #D8B53F — radiant gold with emerging cyan; 6 #168CFF — vibrant electric blue; 7 #183C88 — deep cobalt blue; 8 #111426 — midnight indigo / blue-black; 9 #000000 — pure black.

The background at EVERY level except Level 9 is a soft, cloudy, abstract nebula dominated by that level's color. It should have atmospheric depth, pigment variation and gentle luminosity rather than a flat fill. The palette moves from very light warm tones through yellow, orange and gold, peaks in vibrant electric blue at Level 6, then darkens through cobalt and midnight indigo. PURE BLACK / TOTAL DARKNESS IS RESERVED EXCLUSIVELY FOR LEVEL 9. Levels 7 and 8 must remain visibly blue/indigo rather than black.

## Experiment direction — A — Geometric Orb
Treat the ORB ITSELF as the evolving magical construction. Complexity should be expressed through its surface, shells, intersecting spherical layers, orbital geometry, bands, facets and spatial relationships. Keep the orb substantial and clearly spherical at every level. Levels 1–6 progress from rough/simple to extraordinarily intricate geometry; Levels 7–9 progressively discard that geometry until only sublime celestial simplicity remains. Do not turn the image into a flat spell circle or technical diagram.

## Shared visual language
Show one centered, isolated orb, front-facing or presented with minimal perspective only where needed to communicate spherical depth. Keep a strong readable silhouette and generous negative space. The image should be iconic at card size while retaining painterly atmospheric richness at full resolution.

Modern high-fantasy abstraction with subtle traditional painterly texture: soft pigment, luminous haze, controlled bloom, elegant edges, and mysterious depth. The object represents magical CAPACITY, not any one spell.

Do not include characters, hands, creatures, weapons, landscapes, architecture, text, letters, numbers, runes, glyphs, written symbols, decorative borders, frames, UI, literal planets, literal galaxies, obvious spell-circle diagrams, or recognizable occult symbols. Do not depict literal elemental effects such as flames, lightning bolts or ice. Color may evoke particular magical intensities without making the slot represent a specific spell.

## Current level — 1: Awakening
Background anchor: #DED7C5, dirty eggshell / warm ivory.

A substantial but comparatively small orb, roughly one third of the image width. Simple, imperfect and clearly magical, with only rudimentary structure. Keep it quiet and low-contrast, with generous cloudy atmosphere. It must not read as a tiny seed: the orb is already the unmistakable subject.

The current image must clearly occupy Level 1's position relative to ALL eight other levels. Do not borrow the maximum complexity of Level 6 unless this is Level 6; do not borrow the radical simplicity or true blackness of Level 9 unless this is Level 9.

## Composition
Vertical 5:7 portrait. One orb only. No card mockup. Keep the orb and any associated aura comfortably inside the crop. Preserve enough negative space that the image remains useful as deck artwork. The orb may grow across the series, but even Level 1 should command the composition rather than appearing as a tiny distant dot.

## Output
Vertical 5:7 portrait, at least 750 × 1050 px. Independent artwork asset, not a card mockup.
